newsitem.title: CHINA: Quake jolts big China city, no casualties reported.
newsitem.headline: Quake jolts big China city, no casualties reported.

text.p: An earthquake measuring 5.2 on the Richter scale rocked an area of the southwestern Chinese city of Chongqing on Wednesday, but there were no reports of casualties, officials said.
The earthquake hit the county of Rongchang in Chongqing at 4.13 p.m. (0813 GMT), damaging some buildings in the area, an official with the State Seismological Bureau in Beijing said.
"Some buildings were damaged...it caused cracks in some houses," the official said.
"So far we have no reports of any casualties," he said.
Seismological officials in Chongqing said the earthquake had struck a rural part of the municipality, which is home to nearly 30 million people in both urban and rural areas.
"We have teams out investigating the situation right now," one official said by telephone.
Other municipal officials said Chongqing, on the upper reaches of the Yangtze River, is frequently rocked by minor tremors.
Experts say China is passing through a period of high seismological activity and reports of moderate tremors are common, although most occur in lightly populated areas.
However, China's arid desert region of Xinjiang has been hit with several deadly tremors this year.
About 50 people have been killed this year in a series of earthquakes that have rocked the far-flung northwestern region that is home to many cotton farmers and shepherds.
China suffered the worst quake in modern history on July 28, 1976, when a quake measuring 7.8 hit the northeastern city of Tangshan, killing at least 240,000 people.
The most devastating earthquake in recorded history hit China's Shaanxi province in 1556, killing 830,000 people.
